My washing machine broke down, still well within its warranty.
I figured getting it fixed would be a quick, mildly annoying phone call, and then someone would show up and fix it.
I called the company, explained the issue, and got transferred three separate times.
I landed on someone who took down all my information again, as if the previous two people hadn't written anything down at all.
Each transfer came with its own hold music, a slightly different, equally terrible tune.
By the third transfer I could genuinely hum along without even trying, a skill nobody should ever actually need.
They scheduled a technician for the following week, which felt reasonable enough.
Except the technician never actually showed up, and nobody called to explain why.
I waited around for absolutely nothing all afternoon, staring at my broken machine like it might somehow fix itself out of sheer boredom.
I called back, more annoyed this time.
I was told, very calmly, that there was no record of any appointment ever being scheduled, despite the confirmation text still sitting right there on my phone.
This cycle repeated itself, somehow, three separate times over the following two weeks.
Each call started from scratch, explaining the same broken machine to someone new who promised this time would be different.
Each new person sounded genuinely sympathetic too, apologizing sincerely for the mix-up.
That almost made it worse, honestly, since clearly nobody was actually doing anything to fix it, no matter how kind they all sounded.
By the third week, I had genuinely memorized my warranty number and could recite my address without thinking.

I'd developed something close to a personal relationship with the hold music, complete with the little pauses where the automated voice cut in, right before the same tinny saxophone riff started up again.
Finally, a technician actually showed up.
He looked at the machine for about four minutes and fixed it with what seemed like one small part, casually mentioning this exact issue happens all the time.
I asked why it had taken three weeks and four phone calls for a four-minute fix.
He just shrugged, said scheduling was "a whole separate department," and packed up his tools before heading right back out to his van.
I've since learned to request a confirmation email after every single call, keeping my own paper trail.
I've also started saving screenshots of every confirmation text, just in case, which feels excessive until you remember that one appliance turned into a three-week saga over a single missing part.
My roommate now just calls it "the washing machine incident" whenever it comes up.
